Replay

Cooperative body ownership

Record accepted Godot body observations and track who may produce them before and after a handoff.

3 min readOdin × GodotPage source ↓
On this page ↓
Transport and admissionHandoff and resetAcceptance sequenceCavecrawl profileReliable interaction context

This contract explains how Replay records externally simulated motion and transfers its producer between participants. The acceptance sequence retains the M4 implementation scope; see progress for passed gates.

An engine-owned body is an external observation producer. A Godot solver may run on the currently authorized participant; Replay records accepted pose/velocity samples and gameplay decisions in its ordinary value world. Replaying those values does not rewind or reproduce Godot's contact solver. Deterministic P2P remains a separate profile. Historical gameplay queries may use recorded accepted values, but cannot substitute a current engine query for a historical dynamic collision query.

Transport and admission#

The authoritative runner supports an explicit Latest_Observation control policy. Normal scheduled input remains the default. The policy participates in the existing session/checkpoint contract hash, so peers must agree before play. Latest samples are coalesced into the next authority tick; they are not queued until a predicted client tick. Sender identity, connection generation, epoch, serial, bounds and monotonic input-frontier validation still apply. A separate bounded single-observation packet avoids transmitting a padded multi-tick command window. Scheduled contracts and archive/wire layouts remain compatible with the existing default profile. One-shot gameplay actions keep their existing sequenced acceptance/outcome semantics.

The owner protocol stores its state as values independently of Godot and the transport. Each body stores its current owner, epoch/revision, last accepted sample sequence/source tick, authority acceptance tick, complete value, and an optional pending handoff. An authenticated sender's seat is supplied separately from the sample. Samples cannot name another owner. Finite-value, world-bound and motion predicates are application policy, not proof that an untrusted peer honestly ran the solver.

Handoff and reset#

An offer reserves a new monotonically increasing revision and carries the current complete pose/linear/angular velocity as the preparation baseline. The old owner remains the accepted source while the proposed owner prepares. The first valid sample for the reserved revision commits the transfer at an authority tick. Old-revision samples then fail. Offers can expire or be canceled; canceled revisions are never reused. The game remains responsible for eligibility/proximity arbitration.

Explicit cuts, owner revocation and authority-epoch changes preserve or replace a specified complete value and invalidate prior sample scopes. Checkpoints contain the ownership/offer/frontier state as part of the world. A fresh engine adapter seeds its transform and both velocities from that value, then resumes observation production with the appropriate sequence. Solver contact caches are not preserved; any settling/grace behavior must be explicit.

The initial Godot 2D adapter imposes rigid-body states through PhysicsServer, freezes observers, and separates local solver state from presentation smoothing. Provisional possession may run a speculative local solver, but only an authority-issued revision can publish accepted samples. Score, goals, inventory and other shared decisions remain ordinary authority gameplay over accepted values.

Acceptance sequence#

  1. Native latest-observation policy tests, contract mismatch and archive/recovery checks, preserving existing scheduled-input gates.
  2. Native owner-state tests: prepare/commit, cancellation, expiry, old-owner and recycled-entity rejection, monotonic samples, atomic validation, epoch recovery.
  3. Real Godot 2D solver adapter and separate Replay Slopball port: autonomous character ownership, ball handoff with momentum, goals and three-process viewing.
  4. Prediction/smoothing, reconnect and migrating physics acceptance, matched against the original feel/scenario ledger. Then the same primitives and a separate 3D port.

Original Slopball, Slopball3D, Kit and their assets/run commands remain independently available. Assets reused by a Replay port require provenance and hashes. A synthetic pose test does not establish physics-game parity or the completed M4 milestone.

Cavecrawl profile#

The separate owner-motion Cavecrawl composes the existing gameplay World with versioned avatar/relic observations. It shares inventory/combat/progression code with the server-simulated C8 port while keeping a distinct content contract and isolated app state. The original manual producer supplies poses; this is not an engine-physics or deterministic-P2P claim. Native interaction/handoff/migration and typed service-checkpoint gates are recorded in the acceptance result. Local Chrome migration and saves pass with actual RTC traffic and isolated storage. Other browsers/public networks, full original-rule/presentation parity and paired ergonomic comparison remain open.

Reliable interaction context#

Scoped action context separates an action's claimed owner pose from the coalesced motion stream. Cavecrawl O2 uses issued positions for range checks and the original 64-pixel throw-origin leash, without moving its current avatar pose. The acceptance result includes real suppressed-motion/reliable-action delivery, overtaking motion, old-scope refusal, checkpoint preservation and explicit O1 conversion. This is cooperative claimed context, not a certified historical collision query.
